overview.title: Small cove, big reputation
overview.p1: Cala Bonita is one of the first places travellers hear about in Al Hoceima: a compact, sheltered cove with crystal-clear water and a picture-postcard setting just minutes from the town centre.
overview.p2: It is a popular spot during peak summer months, so arriving early in the morning guarantees a much calmer experience and a better spot on the shore. The setting is noticeably more intimate and serene than Quemado’s expansive bay.
overview.p3: Be sure to bring water, as shade and amenities can be limited. Consider pairing your morning cove session with an afternoon stroll through town.

q1.question: How busy does Cala Bonita get?
q1.answer: It can get quite crowded on summer afternoons; visiting in the early morning offers the best experience.

q2.question: Is Cala Bonita good for families?
q2.answer: Yes, its sheltered waters appeal to families, though parents should always supervise children as conditions can vary.

q3.question: How do I get to Cala Bonita?
q3.answer: Access is via local roads; local petit taxis know the drop-off point well and it is just a short drive from the centre.

q4.question: Can you go snorkelling at Cala Bonita?
q4.answer: The clear water makes it a great spot for casual snorkelling on calm days, though there is no formal dive shop directly on the beach.

q5.question: What are the best nearby beach alternatives?
q5.answer: Quemado Beach offers a wider urban sand strip, while Sfiha Beach provides soft sand and open space slightly further along.
